_comment: CANONICAL Sonomos AI-surface registry — the single source of truth for which AI apps/sites/APIs the product covers. Lives in Service-Mesh/sonomos-vocab and is embedded into the `sonomos-vocab` crate (include_str!), so Rust consumers — Proxy (api_hosts → TLS MITM, skip_path_segments → capture scoping, capture_path_allowlist → the per-host ALLOW-list half of capture scoping, api_scan_paths → content scoping) and the proxy shim (api_hosts → fail-closed SNI policy) — get the data AND the canonical host-matching semantics from the crate. JS consumers (Desktop-Extension web_hosts → page-side shim + manifest; Desktop-Frontend 'Protected Surfaces' UI) receive vendored copies via Locke scripts/sync-surfaces.sh. Do NOT hand-edit vendored copies — edit THIS file and re-run the sync. A provider's `id` is the canonical app identity every capture surface must emit (GuardRequest.app → engine provider → detections.ai_provider). See Locke docs/AI-SURFACES.md. COVERAGE IS NOT UNIFORM: being in this file means the product KNOWS about a surface, not that it screens everything a user types on it — a provider's `web_screening` says whether that provider's web_hosts have a screened submission path at all (`web_screening_modes` below defines the values), and a provider's `localhost_screening` says under which routing its `localhost_ports` are screened at all (`localhost_screening_modes` defines those).
_one_rule_that_covers_every_host: The extension screens the BODY of a script-issued fetch/XMLHttpRequest. A prompt that reaches a provider on a URL instead — typed into the browser's address bar, launched from whatever engine the user set as their browser default, followed as a `?q=` deep link, or submitted by a `<form>` (a form submission is a browser NAVIGATION, not a script call, and `method=post` is unhooked exactly like `method=get`) — is disclosed before any page-side code runs. That is true on EVERY host in this file, including the `body` ones: perplexity.ai, kagi.com and duckduckgo.com all publish OpenSearch descriptors so a browser can send prompts to them by navigation, and a surface bot-gated against probing may do the same without us being able to check. So this is a property of the TRANSPORT, not of a site, and no per-site list can express it — which is why the honest form is this one sentence rather than a longer `web_hosts`. Screening it is deferred: see `web_screening_modes.deferred_to_1x`.

host_matching._comment: ONE rule for every host entry in this file (api_hosts, web_hosts, capture_path_allowlist keys), implemented once in `sonomos_vocab::host_matches` and mirrored by the JS consumers: case-insensitive, trailing-dot-stripped, and an entry covers itself and every subdomain of itself (`api.anthropic.com` covers `foo.api.anthropic.com`; `anthropic.com` does NOT cover `notanthropic.com` — label boundaries only). PLUS, since 2026-10-01, a wildcard: an entry label may carry ONE `*`, which stands for a non-empty run of characters WITHIN THAT ONE LABEL and never crosses a dot. `bedrock-runtime.*.amazonaws.com` covers `bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` and not `bedrock-runtime.a.b.amazonaws.com`; `*-aiplatform.googleapis.com` covers `us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com` (a partial label — Google put the region INSIDE the label, where the subdomain rule cannot reach). The wildcard exists for exactly that shape: an API estate whose varying part sits in the MIDDLE of the name. Hand-listing regions shipped four Bedrock regions and left every other one unscreened with nothing recording the gap. The registrable domain is never wildcarded — the last two labels of an entry must be literal (`*.com`, `api.*.com` are refused by `is_valid_host_entry`, linted in-tree by `every_shipped_host_entry_is_well_formed`) — so a wildcard can never swallow an estate this file did not review. A consumer that has not adopted the wildcard (an older JS `hostMatches`) treats a wildcard entry as a literal that matches nothing real: it claims LESS, never more, which is the safe direction, but it is also a coverage gap in that consumer's view — re-vendor and mirror the rule.

skip_path_segments._comment: Request PATHS the proxy must NOT capture/scan, matched as contiguous runs of complete path segments (never naive substrings — /v1/token_usage IS captured, /usage is not). Default is capture-everything (a missed prompt is a PII leak); list only endpoints that provably carry no prompt: telemetry, feature-flag evals, model/registry listings, billing. Observed: Claude Code sent thousands of /api/event_logging/v2/batch telemetry events — ~85% of all detections, almost all false-positive. ["api","frame","deploy"] (Proxy#117) is Claude Code's Artifact publish on api.anthropic.com: /prepare reserves a slug (and may send each file's sha), /direct sends the page files themselves. Scanned leaf-for-leaf (api.anthropic.com has no allow-list and its api_scan_paths name only /v1/messages), a slug or file leaf was masked and every publish came back 400. It is listed knowing /direct carries the PUBLISHED PAGE'S CONTENT, not only metadata: that content goes to the user's own private artifact page, and on the observed traffic (2026-10-02, 3 of 3 publishes) masking it produced no masked page, only a failed publish. The rest of the frame API is NOT skipped — /api/frame/comments/* carries typed prose and /api/frame/db/* carries page data — so the run is three segments, never ["api","frame"].

capture_methods.mitm: Proxy decrypts the TLS-terminated request and redacts the JSON body (api_hosts). Reliable for SDK/CLI/desktop-app API traffic.
capture_methods.extension: Browser extension holds a script-issued request on a web_host and screens its BODY before it leaves the page. Used where MITM is unreliable (anti-bot / JA3 fingerprinting on consumer web apps). It hooks exactly four transports — fetch, XMLHttpRequest, sendBeacon, fetchLater — and holds no webRequest/webNavigation permission, so a top-level navigation passes it unseen. See `_one_rule_that_covers_every_host`.
capture_methods.passthrough: Recognised as AI traffic but not intercepted (e.g. listed for UI/awareness only).

web_screening_modes._comment: Per-provider `web_screening`: whether this provider's web_hosts have a submission path the extension actually screens. ABSENT MEANS "body" — every entry predating this field is body-screened, which is what the extension has always done — so a consumer that has not adopted the field keeps behaving exactly as it does today. A value a consumer does not recognise must be read as NOT screened: protection may never be inferred from a mode you cannot interpret. WHAT THIS FIELD IS NOT: it is not a promise that everything typed on a `body` host is screened — nothing typed into an address bar is screened on any host, per `_one_rule_that_covers_every_host`. The axis here is 'does this surface have a screened submission path at all', which is precisely the question a UI must answer before it offers a protection toggle. Deliberately still two values: a third 'partly' mode would have to be set per site from what we could probe, and the sites that matter most (chatgpt.com, claude.ai, chat.mistral.ai) are bot-gated against probing — so it would encode our probe coverage rather than a property of the surface, which is the same defect this field was added to fix. This is per-PROVIDER because a provider entry is already the unit that shares a capture story; a provider whose hosts genuinely differ is split into two entries (duckduckgo.com sits in `search` while duck.ai is its own provider, for exactly that reason), and `provider_for_host` resolves a host to the entry with the LONGEST matching suffix so a nested split like kagi.com / assistant.kagi.com lands on the right entry regardless of catalog order.
web_screening_modes.body: The extension holds fetch/XHR requests that carry a BODY and screens the exact bytes before they leave the page. That covers chat surfaces, where the prompt IS the POST body.
web_screening_modes.none: This surface has no screened submission path: what a user types here leaves as a top-level navigation (a search box is a GET, or a POST form — both are navigations). Consumers MUST present these as unscreened and MUST NOT offer a toggle that implies protection. THE HOSTS STAY IN `web_hosts` AND MUST NOT BE MOVED OUT OF IT: `web_hosts` drives BOTH the extension's injection list AND the shim's request-target scope set, so deleting a host from here deletes real screening — possibly on a DIFFERENT page, since the shim scopes on the request TARGET (duck.ai's chat XHRs target duckduckgo.com; Kagi Assistant is reached through kagi.com). Anything that does leave one of these hosts as a bodied fetch/XHR is still screened normally; `none` is a statement about what the user types, not a switch.
web_screening_modes.deferred_to_1x: Screening navigation-borne prompts is DEFERRED TO 1.x, and the reason is not plumbing. For chat, masking preserves utility because the model still answers the masked question; for search the PII often IS the query, and searching for `<PERSON_1> <ADDRESS_1>` returns nothing useful. Mask-and-forward — the primitive the whole product rests on — does not transfer. It needs a different interaction model (warn-and-confirm before the navigation commits, an override verdict path, 'sent anyway' event semantics), which is a feature with its own design doc, not a capture hook. Two consequences while it is deferred. (1) DO NOT add search engines to this file to 'improve coverage': every one would be `none`, which buys no protection while costing two content-script match patterns, a UI row, a standing claim and a liveness obligation — this file shipped a dead Phind for seven months. (2) The class cannot be enumerated anyway — Ecosia, Qwant, Startpage, Mojeek, Yandex, Baidu, Naver, Seznam and every self-hosted SearXNG instance are all navigation-borne, and the catalog is CLOSED-WORLD: a host we never name gets no injection, no toggle and no claim, which is already the correct answer for all of them. The general rule is `_one_rule_that_covers_every_host`, stated once; the list is only the surfaces we make a statement about.

localhost_screening_modes._comment: Per-provider `localhost_screening`: how much of a provider's `localhost_ports` traffic the proxy can actually screen. Same discipline as `web_screening`: ABSENT MEANS "explicit-proxy-only" — the only coverage loopback has ever had — so a consumer that has not adopted the field keeps claiming exactly what was true before it existed; a value a consumer does not recognise must be read as NOT screened, because protection may never be inferred from a mode you cannot interpret. And like `web_screening`, this field is about what may be CLAIMED, never a switch: it gates nothing, and no capture, MITM or path-scoping decision reads it (pinned by `declaring_localhost_screening_changes_no_capture_decision`).
localhost_screening_modes.explicit-proxy-only: Screened ONLY when a client is explicitly proxied at the Sonomos proxy — HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY in the environment, or a per-tool --proxy flag. The transparent path does NOT carry loopback traffic: the nftables redirect returns early for loopback (`oifname lo return`) and redirects dport 443 only, so a direct connection to 127.0.0.1:11434 never reaches the proxy, and nothing in Locke sets HTTPS_PROXY for the user. Consumers MUST NOT present these ports as protected by default, and MUST NOT claim local-model traffic is screened without the 'when the client is routed through the proxy' qualifier. Transparent loopback capture (a loopback-scoped redirect rule, shim routing on SO_ORIGINAL_DST, plaintext-HTTP handling) is 1.x work — when it ships it arrives as a NEW mode value, never by silently widening this one.

capture_path_allowlist_semantics._comment: Per-provider `capture_path_allowlist`: the ALLOW-list half of capture scoping, keyed by the HOST it narrows. ABSENT MEANS “capture everything except skip_path_segments” — the conservative default every host has always had — so a consumer that has not adopted the field, and every provider that does not declare it, behaves exactly as before. WHY IT EXISTS: redaction is field-agnostic BY CONSTRUCTION. Spliicer-Guard emits every string leaf of a JSON body (Spliicer-Guard/src/extract/json.rs) and the only stage that may drop one is a DENY-list of 14 protocol key names (Spliicer-Guard/src/classify.rs) whose value half rejects anything containing '@' or whitespace — so an email address or a person's name can never be excluded by it. Measured end to end on the real chain: {'email':'test@gmail.com','password':'hunter2'} is rebuilt as {'email':'EML_n05x','password':'hunter2'} (redaction tokens carry a per-type prefix — EML_, PHN_, SSN_, CCN_, AKY_, PER_ … — since Spliicer#116). Harmless on an api_host that carries Bearer-token completions and nothing else; fatal on a host that carries the user's ACCOUNT traffic on the same hostname as chat (claude.ai also serves sign-in, profile and billing), where a masked email means authentication simply fails. Desktop apps that are web wrappers (Claude desktop → claude.ai, MS Copilot desktop → copilot.microsoft.com) live entirely on such hosts and are screened by nothing today, because the browser extension cannot see inside a native app. This field is the mechanism such a host needs BEFORE it can be promoted into api_hosts; the promotion itself is a separate release decision that still needs an authenticated real-traffic test.
capture_path_allowlist_semantics.keyed_by_host: The key is a host entry, matched with this file's one host-matching rule (case-insensitive, trailing-dot-stripped, exact or subdomain-of); the LONGEST matching key wins. Keyed by host rather than by provider because the risk is a property of the hostname: the anthropic provider owns BOTH api.anthropic.com — an api_host that must keep the capture-everything default — and claude.ai. A provider-wide list could not narrow the second without silently narrowing the first, turning 'capture everything a prompt could hide in' into 'capture only what someone remembered to type', which is a PII leak.
capture_path_allowlist_semantics.matching: Segment-wise, never substrings — the same rule as skip_path_segments and for the same reason (/v1/token_usage is not /usage). '*' is a wildcard for exactly ONE whole segment, because the real prompt endpoints are UUID-bearing: /api/organizations/*/chat_conversations/*/completion. A pattern segment mixing '*' with anything else (chat_*) is MALFORMED and matches nothing — partial-segment matching is the naive-substring bug arriving through the other door. Segment counts must be EQUAL: a pattern is NOT a prefix, because a path with an unanticipated trailing segment is a different endpoint and admitting it is exactly the accident this field exists to prevent (prefix matching stays addable later; it could not be removed later). Matching is ASCII case-insensitive and patterns must be written lowercase. There is NO percent-decoding, so a percent-encoded spelling simply fails to match. Query strings are not part of a path and are never seen.
capture_path_allowlist_semantics.unrecognised_means_passthrough: A path matching no pattern is NOT captured and NOT masked, and neither is a path matched only by a malformed pattern: anything unrecognised claims less, never more — the same discipline as web_screening_modes. Note it does NOT fall back to capture-everything: on a host narrowed for this reason, capture-everything IS the authentication-breaking behaviour, so a data defect must fail toward passthrough rather than toward masking a sign-in. An empty list reads as ABSENT, so a half-written entry (a _comment and no paths) cannot silently switch screening off on a host we decrypt. Malformed patterns are kept out of releases by the crate test every_shipped_capture_path_pattern_is_well_formed.
capture_path_allowlist_semantics.composition_with_skip_path_segments: capture = allowlist_admits(host, path) AND NOT skip_path_segments(path). BOTH, never either: the allow-list narrows and the deny-list still subtracts. Stated allow-then-deny because that is the reading that matters — the DENY-LIST WINS, so a provider cannot re-admit telemetry by naming it in its allow-list, and skip_path_segments stays a global floor no per-provider data can lift.
capture_path_allowlist_semantics.does_not_widen_decryption: Read only about traffic on a host the MITM gate already admitted, and the MITM gate does not read it — the two answers come from disjoint fields. Declaring an allow-list changes which of a host's already-decrypted paths are scanned and rewritten, and nothing else. Declaring one for a host that is still only a web_host is completely inert, which is what lets the mechanism ship ahead of the decision to use it.
capture_path_allowlist_semantics.shape: "capture_path_allowlist": { "_comment": "...", "hosts": { "claude.ai": ["/api/organizations/*/chat_conversations/*/completion"] } }. THREE providers declare one — openai (chatgpt.com), anthropic (claude.ai), perplexity (www.perplexity.ai) — and every one of those three host keys is now in `api_hosts` too, so each list narrows the PROXY as well as the extension. The set is pinned as a whole by the crate test exactly_the_promoted_hosts_declare_a_capture_path_allowlist; read the diff there rather than updating it. (This sentence used to say no provider declared one, which was true only before the 2026-08-25 promotions and #64.)

providers.name: OpenAI / ChatGPT

capture_path_allowlist._comment: chatgpt.com is BOTH an api_host and a web_host, so this list is LIVE to BOTH halves of the product (an_allowlist_on_a_web_only_host_narrows_the_extension_not_the_proxy pins the web-only case; this host is no longer it). It used to read 'INERT to the proxy' and that is now false: the promotion landed in Service-Mesh 31e2a13, 'let one host be both an api_host and a web_host', after 01c5363 had reverted it — so the proxy MITMs chatgpt.com and these are the only paths on it the proxy captures, every other path being decrypted and passed through unread. Its other consumer is the EXTENSION's page-side shim, which otherwise screens every bodied fetch on a screened host. That breaks the site logged-out: /unauth-mweb/sentinel/chat-requirements/finalize carries anti-bot proof-of-work blobs the guard classifies as un-examinable files and fail-closes on, killing the handshake ('Unable to connect'); /unauth-mweb/events/* is telemetry. Neither ever carries the prompt. Admit ONLY the prompt-bearing conversation POSTs: /backend-api/* logged-in, /backend-anon/* logged-out, /unauth-mweb/* logged-out mobile-web. Fixed-segment — sentinel's 4-segment paths and conversation/prepare (3 segments, 'conversation' != 'f') cannot match. Same shape and matching semantics as claude.ai's list, and now the same standing: because chatgpt.com sits in api_hosts, a pattern here whose segment count is wrong is a prompt-bearing endpoint the PROXY passes through unread, not merely one the extension misses. REVIEWED 2026-09-08 alongside the claude.ai upload additions, AND DELIBERATELY NOT WIDENED. The candidate was /backend-api/files, ChatGPT's attachment-create call, plus the conversation endpoints beside it. Three reasons it is not here. (1) NO EVIDENCE IN THIS CATALOG OR THE EXTENSION'S TESTS: unlike claude.ai's uploads — which this file already named, path and all, as a known gap — nothing in the chain records the shape of this endpoint. Locke-Extension tests/shim.test.js pins what is screened and what must pass on this host (the four conversation POSTs screened; sentinel, /api/auth/session, /backend-api/me, /backend-api/settings/user, /unauth-mweb/events/* passing) and /backend-api/files appears in neither list. A pattern's segment count must equal the real path EXACTLY, so an entry written from memory is inert — it screens nothing and reads as though it does, which is worse than an honest gap. (2) IT WOULD NOT REACH THE BYTES ANYWAY: the create call is JSON metadata that returns a signed URL, and the file itself is PUT to blob storage on a DIFFERENT host this catalog does not name. Screening the metadata while the content leaves elsewhere is the shape of assurance that gets counted as coverage. claude.ai is the opposite case — the multipart body goes to claude.ai itself. (3) THE STATED PRINCIPLE HERE IS 'admit ONLY the prompt-bearing conversation POSTs', and widening it needs a real-traffic observation, not an inference. What this needs before it can be added: the observed path and its segment count, and an entry for whatever host receives the bytes. WIDENED 2026-09-17 FOR OPENAI'S CODEX CLI — the sixth pattern, /backend-api/codex/responses, and the first addition to this host since the 2026-08-25 promotion. Codex CLI signed in with a ChatGPT account does not talk to api.openai.com, it talks to THIS host, and none of the five consumer-chat patterns could match its path, so the proxy decrypted those requests and forwarded them UNSCREENED. The path, taken from the upstream source rather than from memory (openai/codex at HEAD, read 2026-09-17): model-provider-info/src/lib.rs declares CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL = 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex', config/defaults.toml declares chatgpt_base_url = 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/', and the prompt endpoint is {base}/responses — codex-api/src/provider.rs Provider::url_for_path joins base and path with a single slash, and both core/src/client.rs and codex-api/src/endpoint/responses.rs record api.path = '/responses'. That is POST /backend-api/codex/responses: THREE fixed segments (backend-api, codex, responses), carrying an OpenAI Responses-API body whose turns live under `input` rather than `messages` — which needs no extractor change, because the guard is field-agnostic and classify.rs already treats `input` as a turn container. THREE FIXED SEGMENTS IS THE WHOLE SCOPING: a literal pattern must equal the real path segment for segment, so this admits that one path and nothing beside it. Its non-prompt siblings stay out and are unreachable by it: /backend-api/codex/models (2 segments after the prefix), /backend-api/codex/alpha/{namespace}/v2/{name} (history notes, 5+), analytics/codex/turn-costs (different prefix entirely), and the account traffic this list has always excluded — /backend-api/me, /backend-api/settings/user, /api/auth/session, sign-in, billing, the sentinel PoW handshake and /unauth-mweb/events/*. Pinned in both directions by the crate test codex_responses_is_screened_without_admitting_its_siblings. WHAT HAD TO CLEAR FIRST, AND DID: Codex zstd-compresses this exact body by default — core/src/client.rs responses_request_compression returns Compression::Zstd whenever request compression is on AND the auth mode uses the Codex backend (protocol/src/auth.rs uses_codex_backend is true for Chatgpt), features/src/lib.rs ships enable_request_compression as Stage::Stable with default_enabled: true, and http-client/src/request.rs sets Content-Encoding: zstd. Until 2026-09-17 neither component could read that body, so admitting this path would have turned an unscreened leak into a 403 on EVERY Codex turn, PII present or not. Both halves now handle it, pure-Rust on both sides (ruzstd), and the guard RE-COMPRESSES the redacted body rather than rewriting the request as identity — Spliicer-Guard docs/RECONSTRUCTION-DECISION.md records why, and note that an identity rewrite was rejected precisely because it could not be validated without the real-traffic test below. WHAT THIS ENTRY STILL OWES: the authenticated real-traffic test this host's promotion has owed since 2026-08-25, which no catalog edit substitutes for. Three things in this entry are inferred from upstream source and not yet observed on the wire: that the live path is exactly these three segments, that the body still arrives Content-Encoding: zstd (rather than gzip, identity, or a comma list, all of which the guard treats differently), and — the only one that can break a working client — that chatgpt.com's origin accepts a REBUILT zstd body, re-compressed by a different encoder than the one that produced it, with a recomputed Content-Length. Until that is run, treat this entry as screened-by-construction, not screened-by-observation. RESIDUAL CODEX GAPS, DELIBERATELY NOT ADDRESSED HERE. (1) NOT REACHABLE BY ANY ALLOW-LIST AT ALL: codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs can carry the same turn over wss:// to the same path, and no request-body path allow-list reaches a WebSocket frame — this is a transport-level gap and needs its own answer. (2) OTHER HOST KEYS, NOT COVERED: chatgpt-staging.com and chat.openai.com are separate keys; chat.openai.com is a web_host here and declares no allow-list, so nothing about this entry reaches either. (3) A USER-CONFIGURABLE BASE URL: chatgpt_base_url is config, so a user who repoints it sends the same turn to a host this catalog may not name. (4) COVERED ONLY BY SUBDOMAIN MATCHING: gov.chatgpt.com inherits this host key's narrowing rather than declaring its own, which is correct today and is a coupling worth knowing about. WIDENED 2026-10-06 FOR ATTACHMENTS (the seventh pattern, /backend-api/files, plus files.oaiusercontent.com as the api_host of its own entry, `openai-files`, directly below). The 2026-09-08 review above asked for two things before this list could take an upload path: the observed path with its segment count, and an entry for the host that receives the bytes. Both are now on file, from public client code and public error reports rather than memory. THE FLOW: (1) POST /backend-api/files with JSON {file_name, file_size, use_case, timezone_offset_min, reset_rate_limits} answers {file_id, upload_url} (lanqian528/chat2api chatgpt/ChatService.py get_upload_url); (2) the file BYTES are PUT, raw, to upload_url with x-ms-blob-type: BlockBlob, an Azure Blob SAS URL (same file, upload()); (3) POST /backend-api/files/{file_id}/uploaded with an empty JSON body (get_download_url_from_upload). THE BYTE HOST is files.oaiusercontent.com: it is the host ChatGPT's own upload error names ('Upload to files.oaiusercontent.com failed', Mozilla bug 1985781 in 2025 and OpenAI community thread 1387059 in 2026-07), it answers Azure's XML ResourceNotFound when fetched bare, OpenAI's network-recommendations help article requires *.oaiusercontent.com, and Locke-Extension tests/shim.test.js has screened the browser half of this same PUT (STORAGE_PUT) since the extension's cross-origin upload scope landed. Before this entry the DESKTOP app and a proxied browser without the extension sent that PUT to a host the proxy did not name, so discovery classed it as non-AI and forwarded it: every ChatGPT attachment left unscreened. NOW: files.oaiusercontent.com is an api_host (entry `openai-files`) with NO allow-list, so every bodied request to it (the PUT) is captured and judged by the one file rule every captured upload gets: text is read and masked, anything the engine cannot read comes back Unsupported and the request is BLOCKED, and an image it cannot examine is withheld behind a placeholder. /backend-api/files is TWO fixed segments and carries the user-authored file NAME, the one copy of the name that otherwise left unscreened (the conversation POST's attachment metadata is already captured); its siblings /backend-api/files/{id}/uploaded (4 segments, empty body) and /backend-api/files/{id} (3, a GET) cannot match. EXACT HOST, NOT THE APEX: oaiusercontent.com also serves the generated-image CDN (sdmntpr*.oaiusercontent.com, GETs) and the sandboxed app and canvas frames (*.web-sandbox.oaiusercontent.com), where screening POSTs made by third-party app code would break them; neither carries the user's upload, so neither is admitted. Pinned by chatgpt_attachments_are_captured_at_the_metadata_call_and_the_byte_host. RESIDUAL: an upload host other than files.oaiusercontent.com (a future regional host) is not captured until it is named here, and this is screened by construction from public descriptions of the traffic, not yet by an authenticated capture.

providers.notes: chatgpt.com is BOTH an api_host and a web_host as of #64 ('let one host be both an api_host and a web_host'): the proxy MITMs it and the capture_path_allowlist above narrows what it captures, while the extension keeps screening the page. THIS FIELD SAID THE OPPOSITE UNTIL 2026-09-17 — that chatgpt.com was web-only and NOT MITM'd — which was true only between the 2026-08-25 promotion's revert (01c5363) and #64, and has read as a false claim of non-interception ever since; the whole point of this file is that a stale claim about coverage is worse than a stated gap. The risks the revert was taken for are unchanged; they are now ACCEPTED POSTURE, the same posture claude.ai and www.perplexity.ai carry. MITM'ing the website means a browser that does not trust the Sonomos CA (Firefox-family keep their own cert store, not the OS one) hits an HSTS cert error, and the fail-closed shim refuses ALL of *.chatgpt.com — sign-in included — whenever the proxy is down; fail-closed and screening hold over TCP/443 only. THE SHIP GATE IS STILL OPEN: the authenticated real-traffic test (sign-in, a chat turn, and a Codex turn, on web AND the desktop app) has not been run against this host. api.openai.com stays a capture-everything api_host; chat.openai.com now 301s to chatgpt.com. Codex CLI on a ChatGPT sign-in lands on this host, and its prompt POST (/backend-api/codex/responses) IS screened as of 2026-09-17, once both components learned to read and rebuild the zstd body Codex sends by default. Screened by construction, not yet by observation: see the allow-list _comment above for what the real-traffic test still has to confirm, and for the residual Codex gaps it does NOT cover — chiefly the WebSocket transport, which no path allow-list reaches.

providers.name: ChatGPT file uploads
providers.notes: ADDED 2026-10-06. The host that receives the BYTES of a ChatGPT attachment: the page (web app, desktop app) PUTs the raw file to an Azure Blob SAS URL on files.oaiusercontent.com that POST chatgpt.com/backend-api/files handed it (flow and sources in the openai allow-list _comment above). Captured with no allow-list, so the PUT is judged by the file rule: text masked, anything unreadable blocked, an unexaminable image withheld. ITS OWN ENTRY, NOT A FOURTH openai api_host, ON PURPOSE: every api_host of a desktop_app provider becomes its own per-host switch, and a switch that did not exist when a profile or a team policy was saved reads as OFF for that profile (Desktop-Frontend proxyDisabledHosts subtracts every app host the saved enabled-set does not name). Inside openai it would have been switched off for every user who ever saved Controls and on every device a pre-existing team policy governs: ChatGPT screened, its attachments not. desktop_app false gives it no switch, so nothing can subtract it: it is screened whenever Locke is, like the aggregators. The cost, accepted: a user who turns ChatGPT off still has its uploads screened (the over-screening direction). Reports attribute these uploads to this entry's name. EXACT HOST: oaiusercontent.com's other subdomains (the sdmntpr* image CDN, *.web-sandbox app frames) carry no upload and stay out.

providers.name: Anthropic / Claude

capture_path_allowlist._comment: claude.ai serves sign-in (/api/auth/send_magic_link carries email_address as a plain string leaf; /api/auth/verify_magic_link carries encoded_email_address), account, billing and conversation reads on the SAME host as chat — field-agnostic redaction there masks the sign-in email and breaks auth. Admit ONLY the two prompt-bearing POSTs. The trailing segment MUST be the literal completion/retry_completion and NEVER '*': /api/organizations/{org}/chat_conversations/{conv}/current_leaf_message_uuid is a 6-segment sibling a trailing wildcard would wrongly admit. The two '*' stand for the org and conversation UUIDs. Covers the claude.ai web app AND both desktop Electron apps (same host+path). ATTACHMENT UPLOADS ADDED (was: a documented residual gap). The two upload paths — /api/{org}/upload (multipart, the attach button on the web app and both desktop Electron apps) and /api/organizations/{org}/convert_document — were excluded on the grounds that "the JSON-leaf engine cannot parse multipart". That reason no longer holds and, while it did, it produced the wrong outcome: an unscreened path is not a smaller version of screening, it is a file leaving the machine unexamined, and NOTHING reported it because nothing was captured. What changed: the guard has a real multipart extractor (Spliicer-Guard crates/sonomos-extract/src/extract/multipart.rs) — a boundary scanner that yields one extract per part, recurses into an application/json part, treats text/* and untyped parts as Text, hands anything else to the file path as File with the part's media type, AND extracts the user-authored filename= out of the Content-Disposition header as its own Text leaf; reconstruction re-frames with boundary repair (handler.rs) and is checked part-by-part by verify_multipart. What the parts then get is the file-coverage.json table: .txt/.md/.csv/.json/source/.log decode and get exactly the detection chat text gets, png/jpeg/webp/gif go through the image pipeline, and the containers that need a parser (.pdf/.docx/.xlsx) fail CLOSED — refused, or withheld behind a same-type placeholder — which is the correct gate behaviour for an unexaminable item and is strictly better than today's silent pass. THE TRAILING SEGMENT IS LITERAL for the same reason as completion: '/api/*/upload' is 3 fixed segments ending in the literal upload, so /api/auth/session and every other 3-segment sibling on this host cannot match, and no wildcard sits last. '/api/*/*' would have admitted the whole of /api. NOT ADDED: /api/organizations/{org}/chat_conversations/{conv}/current_leaf_message_uuid and the other conversation reads — they carry no user-authored bytes.

providers.notes: claude.ai promoted from web_hosts to api_hosts 2026-08-25. api.claude.ai was REMOVED from api_hosts in the SAME edit: it is a subdomain of claude.ai, so listing both fails the redundancy lint no_host_is_listed_twice_and_none_is_redundant_within_its_provider (catalog.rs:1200-1219). ACCEPTED NARROWING (the api.claude.ai apex trap, resolved explicitly because the mechanism cannot resolve it): the allowlist mechanism cannot express a capture-everything key — empty lists read as absent (catalog.rs:352-364), there is no all-paths wildcard, and segment counts must be equal — so once claude.ai is an api_host, EVERY *.claude.ai subdomain, including the removed api.claude.ai, inherits claude.ai's completion-only allowlist rather than capture-everything (subdomain inheritance pinned at catalog.rs:1676-1699). This is safe ONLY because api.claude.ai does not resolve (NXDOMAIN re-verified 2026-08-25); api.anthropic.com remains the capture-everything Claude API host and is untouched. SHIP GATE: re-verify at ship time that api.claude.ai and every *.claude.ai API subdomain is still non-resolving; if api.claude.ai is ever activated as a bearer-token API it would be silently under-captured and this promotion MUST be revisited. ACCEPTED RELEASE POSTURE: the fail-closed shim refuses all of *.claude.ai (sign-in included) when the proxy is down; fail-closed + screening hold over TCP/443 only (QUIC/HTTP-3 bypasses until QUIC_REJECT=1). Claude Code is unaffected (it uses api.anthropic.com, a separate host key). SHIPS ONLY AFTER the authenticated real-traffic test (magic-link sign-in + profile/billing edit + a chat turn, on web AND the desktop app). claude.com / console.anthropic.com stay web_hosts. The prompt is the top-level body.prompt string leaf; turn_message_uuids and create_conversation_params.name (sent empty) carry no PII.

providers.name: Google Gemini / Vertex / AI Studio
providers.notes: GEMINI CLI / CODE ASSIST ADDED 2026-10-01 (second round). `cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com` is the Gemini Code Assist backend that the Gemini CLI uses when signed in with a Google account (the default login path, not an API key): `POST /v1internal:generateContent` and `:streamGenerateContent` carry `{project, model, request: {contents: [...]}}` — the ordinary Gemini request envelope wrapped one level deeper, plain JSON with a Bearer token, so the guard's field-agnostic leaf extraction screens every string it carries (verified 2026-10-01: resolves, answers 401 application/json unauthenticated). A CLI user with an API key goes to generativelanguage.googleapis.com instead, which was already here. NO `api_scan_paths` ENTRY ON PURPOSE: that field is content scoping the guard replaced structurally — an endpoint without one is scanned leaf-for-leaf (Spliicer-Guard `content_scope_for` returns None), which is the capture-everything default every other host in this file gets, and the one a wrapped envelope needs. ---- VERTEX AI REGIONAL ENDPOINTS ADDED 2026-10-01. The Vertex SDKs (google-cloud-aiplatform; google-genai with vertexai=True) default to `{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com` — `us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com` and so on — and only the global endpoint is `aiplatform.googleapis.com`. `us-central1-aiplatform` is ONE label, not a subdomain of `aiplatform`, so the entry that was here never reached a single regional call: the dominant Vertex shape was undecrypted and, because nothing was captured, never showed up as a gap. `*-aiplatform.googleapis.com` covers every region (see `host_matching`); `storage.googleapis.com` and the rest of the googleapis estate are untouched, because the wildcard is confined to the one label and the literal `-aiplatform` tail must be present. ---- UNVERIFIED, AND THE ONLY FIRST-HAND EVIDENCE CONTRADICTS IT. This entry has said since the crate's first commit that Gemini web/app traffic often uses protobuf/RPC (not plain JSON), so the generic JSON scan may not see the prompt and web masking needs per-surface decoding (1.x). That sentence has been copied forward unchanged and was never derived from a capture: there is no fixture, HAR, test or comment behind it anywhere in the fleet. Against it, the Sonomos browser extension shipped a WORKING Gemini masker in 2026-03 whose own notes say Gemini web sends a form-encoded f.req field carrying nested JSON (the batchexecute/RPC envelope) -- a shape the guard's existing form and multipart extractors already surface as a scannable text leaf. The observed behaviour argues against protobuf too: an undecodable body does NOT silently yield zero detections. The guard screens it as one opaque blob, the engine returns Unsupported, and withhold cannot withhold a non-image, so every Gemini prompt would hard-fail with a visible refusal -- which nobody has reported. DO NOT build a protobuf decoder off this note: capture one real Gemini web body first (Spliicer-Guard docs/HARVEST.md, ZenHub #139) and replay it. The two readings imply completely different work -- a new binary codec, versus no new extractor at all plus a possible over-masking guard on the RPC envelope. See ZenHub #173. The API hosts are standard JSON and MITM-redactable now. NOTE the caveat this entry has always carried: `web_screening: body` says the prompt travels as a body we HOLD, not that we can always read it — a held body we cannot decode is screened in transport and unscreened in effect. Google Search itself is a separate `search` entry: it is a different surface with a different answer.

That is an over-claim of the same family as the search one — a screened claim on a host with nothing to screen — with the real surface uncovered. console.x.ai is the developer console.

providers.name: Perplexity

capture_path_allowlist._comment: www.perplexity.ai carries sign-in/session (/api/auth/*), settings, subscription and upload metadata under /rest/* on the SAME host as chat — admit ONLY the single prompt-bearing SSE endpoint (the ask box POSTs JSON, replies stream as SSE). Keyed at www.perplexity.ai and NOT the apex perplexity.ai on purpose: host_matches('perplexity.ai','api.perplexity.ai') is TRUE, so an apex key would also narrow the shipped, LIVE v1 api_host api.perplexity.ai from capture-everything to this one path — decrypted but never captured = a silent PII leak on real completion traffic. www.perplexity.ai does not match api.perplexity.ai, so api.perplexity.ai keeps the capture-everything default. Covers the Perplexity Windows/Mac desktop app and the Comet browser (same /rest/sse/perplexity_ask endpoint), both invisible to the extension. REVIEWED 2026-09-08 alongside the claude.ai upload additions, AND DELIBERATELY NOT WIDENED. This entry already names upload metadata under /rest/* among the things it excludes ON PURPOSE, next to sign-in, settings and subscription — that is a decision this file recorded, not an oversight to correct. Perplexity's attachment flow takes a pre-signed S3 POST policy from /rest/uploads/create_upload_url (or batch_create_upload_urls) and POSTs a multipart form, signing fields plus the file, to storage on a host this catalog does not name (ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws.com for documents, Cloudinary for images), so admitting the metadata call would screen the request that carries no file. In the browser the extension holds that form by its FILE part, whatever its destination (Locke-Extension content/shim.js isUploadScope, 2026-10-06), so the bytes are screened there and nothing about this entry has to change for it. The desktop app's upload through the proxy is NOT covered: the bucket host is shared S3 and Cloudinary infrastructure this catalog does not name. And the keying constraint is sharper here than anywhere else in this file: the key MUST stay www.perplexity.ai, because host_matches('perplexity.ai', 'api.perplexity.ai') is TRUE and an apex key would narrow the live api_host api.perplexity.ai down to whatever this list says — decrypted but never captured, a silent leak on real completion traffic. Anything added here must be observed on www.perplexity.ai specifically.

providers.notes: www.perplexity.ai promoted into api_hosts 2026-08-25 (the sibling of the apex, NOT the apex). WHY: keying at perplexity.ai would narrow the live api_host api.perplexity.ai (verified resolving 2026-08-25) — the exact silent-leak defect — AND api_hosts ['api.perplexity.ai','perplexity.ai'] would fail the redundancy lint; deleting api.perplexity.ai instead would silence the lint while KEEPING the leak, and an empty override key cannot help (empty lists are dropped, catalog.rs:357-361). desktop_app set true so the promoted app surface renders a Controls row/toggle rather than being decrypted invisibly (side effect: api.perplexity.ai now renders a UI row too). ACCEPTED: the perplexity.ai web_host's *.perplexity.ai extension injection still covers www.perplexity.ai, so the WEB app is double-covered (extension + proxy) — benign redundancy (already-redacted tokens — per-type prefixes EML_, PHN_, SSN_, CCN_, AKY_, PER_ … since Spliicer#116 — are not re-detected); the net new coverage is the desktop app + Comet, which only the proxy can reach. The fail-closed shim refuses www.perplexity.ai (its sign-in included) when the proxy is down — www-scoped, the apex perplexity.ai is unaffected; fail-closed + screening hold over TCP/443 only (QUIC bypass until QUIC_REJECT=1). SHIPS ONLY AFTER the authenticated real-traffic test, which MUST confirm the default web/desktop/Comet clients submit chat to www.perplexity.ai and HALT the promotion if any default client uses the apex perplexity.ai for chat. Perplexity also ships /opensearch.xml with a GET `{searchTerms}` template and honours /search?q= (both verified 2026-08-18), so it can be registered as a browser's default engine and prompted by navigation — unscreened, like every other surface in this file. That is `_one_rule_that_covers_every_host`, not a Perplexity-specific fact, and it is deliberately NOT encoded as a per-site mode: see `web_screening_modes._comment`.

No api_hosts here: Azure OpenAI is a different product on different hosts and has its own entry, `azure-openai` (this note used to say per-resource `{resource}.openai.azure.com` 'cannot be one safe entry'; the apex rule covers it — see that entry). providers.name: Azure OpenAI / Azure AI Foundry
providers.notes: ADDED 2026-10-01. Azure OpenAI is per-resource — `{resource}.openai.azure.com` — which the `microsoft` entry recorded as 'cannot be one safe entry'. It can, by the same reasoning as `githubcopilot.com`: the apex `openai.azure.com` names no server at all (NXDOMAIN, verified 2026-10-01) and every subdomain of it is an Azure OpenAI data-plane endpoint, so under the subdomain rule the apex covers every resource without naming any — and unlike `github.com` or `azure.com`, nothing else lives under it. Sign-in is login.microsoftonline.com, the portal is portal.azure.com, management is management.azure.com; none of those is reached by these entries. THREE apexes because one resource answers under three names: `{resource}.openai.azure.com` (the Azure OpenAI endpoint the openai SDKs default to), `{resource}.cognitiveservices.azure.com` (the Azure AI Services / AI Foundry resource endpoint, which also serves the /openai/* routes) and `{resource}.services.ai.azure.com` (AI Foundry's /models inference and agents). Bodies are plain JSON with Bearer/api-key auth — MITM-redactable exactly like api.openai.com, no signature over the body. CAVEAT, cognitiveservices.azure.com: that apex also carries the NON-LLM Azure AI services (Speech, Vision, Document Intelligence, Translator, Language) on the same per-resource hostnames. Their JSON bodies (translation, language) are screened like any text. Their BINARY bodies — audio, PDFs, images for OCR — reach the guard's file gate, where a type the engine cannot examine fails CLOSED and the request is refused (file-coverage.json `blocked`). That is the gate's stated posture for an unexaminable item, not a silent miss — but it means an Azure Document Intelligence or Speech call through the proxy is refused rather than forwarded. If that is wrong for a deployment, the surface is switchable through the subtractive override like any api_host. SEPARATE id from `microsoft` on purpose: that entry is Microsoft Copilot on the web; one id for both would put two products in one metrics row (the anthropic-vs-claude drift again). ROOT HELPER: there is nothing for `sonomos-redirect reset-uncovered` to resolve for these — the apex has no address and resource names are unknowable — so pre-arm connections to an Azure OpenAI resource are not reset; Proxy `tests/redirect_helper_api_hosts_test.rs` records that as an accepted, stated residual rather than listing an unresolvable name.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.notes: copilot-proxy.githubusercontent.com ADDED 2026-10-01: the ORIGINAL Copilot completions proxy (`/v1/engines/copilot-codex/completions`, the file prefix/suffix as the JSON `prompt`), still live and still what older plugin builds — JetBrains and Neovim releases that predate the move to proxy.individual.githubcopilot.com — send inline completions to (verified 2026-10-01: resolves, answers 401 on that path with Copilot's own CORS header set naming Copilot-Integration-Id, Editor-Version, Openai-Intent). A pre-catalog guard arm once named it beside api.githubcopilot.com and the migration dropped both; the apex restored one. ONE SUBDOMAIN, NEVER THE APEX: githubusercontent.com also serves raw.githubusercontent.com, avatars., objects., user-images. — every raw file and image GitHub hands out — and the subdomain rule on the apex would MITM all of it. GitHub Models (models.github.ai) is a different product with its own entry. ADDED 2026-08-28. GitHub Copilot's API traffic was in NO catalog entry, so it matched no provider, took the default surface profile and was never screened -- and because nothing was captured it did not show up as an unprotected surface either, it simply never appeared. The pre-catalog guard had a copilot arm reached by api.githubcopilot.com; the migration to this file dropped the host, and Spliicer-Guard's surface_profile.rs has carried a comment saying so ever since. SEPARATE FROM microsoft ON PURPOSE: that entry is Microsoft Copilot on copilot.microsoft.com, a different product on a different host with a different transport. One id for both would put two products in one metrics row, which is the anthropic-vs-claude drift again in the other direction. THE APEX IS DELIBERATE: host_matches means an entry covers itself and every subdomain, and the whole of githubcopilot.com is Copilot -- so this one line covers api., proxy.individual., proxy.business., proxy.enterprise. and any variant GitHub adds, without us enumerating hosts we have not observed. That is the opposite of the search entry listing www.google.com rather than google.com, where the apex would have swallowed an unrelated estate. NO web_hosts: Copilot on the web lives at github.com/copilot, and github.com serves sign-in, billing, repositories and the whole site on that same name. Field-agnostic redaction would mask an email in a sign-in body and break authentication -- exactly the case capture_path_allowlist exists for. A web surface here needs that allow-list first, and a real-traffic test; it is not covered by this entry. desktop_app is true because Copilot runs inside editors (VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio), which the browser extension cannot see -- MITM is the only route to this surface.

The apex github.com is never the entry (sign-in, billing, the whole site), and models.github.ai answered this check's unauthenticated probe with a bare `OK` edge response rather than a JSON 401 — the host is GitHub's (140.82.x) and the endpoint is the documented one, but an observed real-traffic capture is still the thing that confirms the body shape, as for every entry here.

Free.') and its prompt leaves as a bodied POST the extension holds — it sat under `search` by brand association, so declaring that entry `none` would have told users a working, screened surface was unprotected AND removed the only toggle they had over it. DO NOT REMOVE duckduckgo.com FROM THE `search` ENTRY: duck.ai's chat XHRs target duckduckgo.com (verified — POST https://duckduckgo.com/duckchat/v1/chat answers, and duck.ai's CSP connect-src names duckduckgo.com), and the shim scopes on the REQUEST TARGET host, so dropping it would silently stop screening this chat. duckduckgo.com's own search box is a navigation and stays unscreened: two pages, two truths, two entries.

Kagi's other surface, the kagi.com search box, is NOT screened and stays in `search` — note its homepage form is `method=post`, which looks bodied but is a browser NAVIGATION, not a script-issued fetch: the shim hooks no submit event and no form element, so it is unhooked exactly like a GET. assistant.kagi.com is also a subdomain of the `search` entry's kagi.com, which is why `provider_for_host` resolves the LONGEST matching entry rather than the first one in catalog order.

providers.name: AWS Bedrock
providers.notes: FIPS ENDPOINTS ADDED 2026-10-01 (second round): `bedrock-runtime-fips.{region}.amazonaws.com` is the SAME runtime API (InvokeModel, Converse, the streaming pair) on AWS's FIPS 140 endpoint — identical paths, identical bodies, identical SigV4 posture — which an SDK selects with `use_fips_endpoint` / `AWS_USE_FIPS_ENDPOINT=true`, routinely in GovCloud and regulated deployments. `bedrock-runtime-fips` is one label, not a subdomain of `bedrock-runtime`, so the wildcard entry never reached it (verified 2026-10-01: bedrock-runtime-fips.us-east-1 resolves and answers 403 application/json unsigned). `bedrock-agent-runtime.{region}` (InvokeAgent, RetrieveAndGenerate) is STILL NOT ADDED — a different API whose body shapes have not been observed, as recorded below; it is the next candidate once a capture exists. EVERY REGION SINCE 2026-10-01. This entry used to list four regions by hand and say 'other regions added by operators via config' — but the override is subtractive and there is no such config, so a request to bedrock-runtime.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com matched no entry, was never decrypted, and never appeared as a gap because nothing was captured. `bedrock-runtime.*.amazonaws.com` covers `bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com` for every region, with the `*` confined to the one region label (see `host_matching`), so `s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` and the rest of AWS are untouched. NOT covered, deliberately: `bedrock.{region}` is the control plane (model listings, no prompts) and `bedrock-agent-runtime.{region}` (InvokeAgent) is not added without an observed body; the FIPS variants `bedrock-runtime-fips.{region}` are likewise unlisted. SIGV4 — READ BEFORE RELYING ON MASKING HERE. Bedrock requests are SigV4-signed and the signature commits to the SHA-256 of the request body. The guard forwards a CLEAN body byte-for-byte (Spliicer-Guard handler: 'clean ⇒ allow, original bytes, untouched'), so clean traffic is unaffected by screening. A body with a detection is spliced, so the signature no longer matches and AWS refuses the request with 403 InvalidSignatureException. The MASKED bytes are what left the machine; the original never did. So in effect this surface is fail-closed-at-origin rather than mask-and-forward: a Bedrock request carrying PII does not succeed, and the user sees AWS's signature error rather than a Sonomos verdict. Nothing is silent — the proxy logs the redaction and the client gets a hard 403 — but the error is the wrong one. There is no catalog field today for 'this body is integrity-signed; refuse locally with an explanation instead of forwarding a doomed request' (the guard's surface profile is optimisation-only by design and may never reduce screening). Adding one is a Proxy-side follow-up; until then this entry states the limitation rather than hiding the surface.

providers.name: Stability AI
providers.notes: ADDED 2026-10-01. Image generation and editing. Prompts travel as multipart/form-data fields (v2beta) or JSON (v1), both of which the guard's extractors surface as text leaves; image parts go through the image pipeline.

providers.name: ElevenLabs
providers.notes: ADDED 2026-10-01. Text-to-speech: /v1/text-to-speech/* carries the text to be spoken as a JSON string leaf — screened exactly like a prompt, since that text is what leaves the machine. Speech-to-text uploads are multipart with an audio part; audio is a type the engine cannot examine, so that part fails CLOSED at the guard's file gate and the request is refused (file-coverage.json `blocked`) rather than forwarded unexamined.

providers.name: AssemblyAI
providers.notes: ADDED 2026-10-01. /v2/transcript (JSON: audio_url plus options) and LeMUR (/lemur/v3/*, JSON prompts over transcripts) are screened as text. /v2/upload posts RAW AUDIO BYTES — an opaque body the engine cannot examine fails CLOSED at the guard's file gate and the request is refused, which is the gate's stated posture for an unexaminable item, not a silent pass. A deployment that uploads audio through the proxy will see those uploads refused unless this surface is switched off through the override.

providers.name: Deepgram
providers.notes: ADDED 2026-10-01. Speech-to-text /v1/listen takes either `{"url": ...}` JSON (screened as text) or RAW AUDIO BYTES — the latter is an opaque body the engine cannot examine, so it fails CLOSED at the guard's file gate and is refused (same posture as AssemblyAI's /v2/upload). Text-to-speech /v1/speak carries the text to be spoken as JSON and is screened like a prompt.

providers.name: Voyage AI
providers.notes: ADDED 2026-10-01. Embeddings and rerankers: `input`, `query` and `documents` are the user's own text as JSON leaves — the whole document corpus a RAG pipeline indexes passes through here, which is why an embeddings host is a screening surface and not just a utility.

providers.name: Jina AI
providers.notes: ADDED 2026-10-01. Embeddings, reranker and classifier — JSON text leaves, same shape and same reasoning as Voyage. Jina's reader/search hosts (r.jina.ai, s.jina.ai) take a URL rather than user text and are NOT listed.

providers.name: JetBrains AI Assistant
providers.notes: ADDED 2026-10-06 (catalog-ides). Cursor and Windsurf were listed beside it the same day and REMOVED by review (R3): their backends speak protobuf (Connect and gRPC; Cursor's chat is an HTTP/2 stream whose request half stays open), and the guard has no protobuf parser. Through the real bridge -> guard -> engine chain every chat, Tab and completion body, clean or not, came back Block ("could not be examined"), and the proxy buffers a screened body to its end, so a request stream that stays open is never forwarded at all. Listing them would switch both editors off for every Locke user; they stay out (a disclosed known limitation) until the guard reads protobuf and the proxy screens a stream, and `protobuf_ide_backends_stay_out_of_the_catalog` pins it. JetBrains AI sends JSON (chat at /user/v5/llm/chat/stream/...) and is screened like any JSON API. Hosts: the JetBrains AI service base URLs, as JetBrains publishes them for administrators who block AI at the network level (jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/disable-ai-assistant.html): api.jetbrains.ai, api.app.prod.grazie.aws.intellij.net (the Grazie backend the AI Assistant and Junie call) and api.ai.jetbrains.com.cn (Mainland China). Never jetbrains.com or account.jetbrains.com, which carry licensing and downloads. The IDE (unlike a bare JVM) uses the system proxy by default (Auto-detect) and trusts the OS certificate store (jetbrains.com/help/idea/ssl-certificates.html: the Windows store, and /etc/ssl/certs and /etc/pki/tls/certs on Linux), so a default install is reached on Windows by the system proxy and on Linux by the redirect; an IDE set to a manual proxy or to no proxy is not: see Proxy deploy/os-proxy/WINDOWS.md (JetBrains IDEs). GitHub Copilot inside a JetBrains IDE is the github-copilot entry. Not verified against live traffic from this environment.

providers.name: Web search (navigation-borne queries)
providers.notes: NOT A LIST OF SEARCH ENGINES TO BE COMPLETED — see `web_screening_modes.deferred_to_1x` before adding one. These are surfaces the product already injects on whose only submission path is a top-level navigation, so nothing a searcher types on them is screened; the entry exists so no consumer presents them as protected. PRUNED 2026-08-18 after live probing: brave.com (Brave's marketing site — 'The browser that puts you first' — not the engine; search.brave.com is, and the apex bought a `*.brave.com` injection pattern across Brave's entire web estate for zero screening), leo.brave.com (no DNS record at all, and Brave Leo is a browser-native sidebar — structurally unreachable by a content script under ANY permission model, not merely unscreened), phind.com and www.phind.com (Phind shut down 2026-01-16; www.phind.com was in any case already subsumed by phind.com under the subdomain rule). duck.ai and assistant.kagi.com moved OUT to their own entries because they are screened. KEPT DELIBERATELY: duckduckgo.com and kagi.com — their own search boxes are navigations, but those hostnames also carry the chat traffic of the two entries above, and the shim scopes on the request target, so removing either would delete real screening on a different page. you.com is kept and claims nothing: its homepage is now an API pitch ('The Leading Web Search APIs for AI') and the consumer chat is login-gated, so 'we screen nothing you typically type here' is the honest reading, and any bodied chat that does happen is still screened per the `none` mode.

providers.name: Local model servers
providers.notes: Default ports of the local model servers that expose an OpenAI-compatible (or Ollama-native) HTTP API on loopback: Ollama 11434, LM Studio 1234 (its local server, `/v1/chat/completions`), Jan 1337 (its built-in API server), GPT4All 4891 (its local API server, off by default), koboldcpp 5001 (its KoboldAI/OpenAI-compatible API). The four after Ollama were ADDED 2026-10-01; each is that product's documented default and is distinctive enough that no common dev server squats on it. DELIBERATELY NOT LISTED: 8080, 8000, 3000, 5000 and the rest of the generic dev-server ports — llama.cpp's `llama-server` (8080), vLLM (8000), text-generation-webui (5000/7860) and LocalAI (8080) all default to a port that an ordinary web app, notebook or framework dev server also uses, and a loopback port in this list is MITM'd for EVERY client that is explicitly proxied, so naming one would decrypt and screen unrelated local traffic. The Proxy's local-surfaces override is SUBTRACTIVE only — it can switch a listed port off, never add one — so a local server on one of those generic ports is simply not screened today, and this note records that rather than hiding it. Screened only when a client is explicitly proxied via HTTP(S)_PROXY/--proxy; the transparent path does not carry loopback traffic (the nftables redirect has `oifname lo return` and a dport-443-only scope, and nothing in Locke sets HTTPS_PROXY). This entry used to say 'Loopback, MITM-redactable', which every consumer honestly rendered as protected-by-default — the same over-claim family as the search one. See `localhost_screening_modes`.
